correctness.rationale: For a Frobenius-stable six-point conic divisor and the stated incidence-genericity condition, classical Kirkman concurrency and Pascal theory identify the sixty unlabeled hexagons, sixty corresponding Kirkman points, and their 180 edge-disjoint incidences. The standalone exact-integer verifier re-derives all 11 cycle-type orbit spectra by enumerating the 720 group elements; fixed-point calculations over powers and all group elements give independent finite consistency checks. A separate exact projective construction with six rational conic points verifies the exact 180 incidences over Q and F_10007, supporting the normalization but not substituting for the classical theorem or the exhaustive group action. Finite étale descent then establishes the zeta functions, rational non-incidence cases and minimal splitting degrees. Assertions are conditional on geometric generality; no extrapolation to all small-field configurations.

originality.rationale: The 60 Pascal lines, 60 Kirkman points and 3-regular incidence are known; novelty is not asserted for these antecedents. The assessed contribution explicitly classifies the 180 incidence flags by all eleven finite-field Frobenius partitions, identifies exactly the two rational non-incidence obstructions, and provides extension-field point counts and zeta functions. Originality comparisons were made to the content/implications of closely relevant full text and to actual mathematical-record search hits; no source located states or tabulates the all-partition arithmetic result. The arithmetic table is computable from the known equivariant structure, and older full texts were not all inspected, so an unindexed implicit/published table remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Conway–Ryba 2012 and 2013 full texts were unavailable; no conclusion of NON_COVERING is made for unread sections.
The complete S6-equivariant incidence model is classical, and an unindexed or indirectly titled earlier arithmetic orbit table could subsume the explicit eleven rows.
The result is conditional on an incidence-generic sextuple and does not prove realization for every splitting pattern over every small finite field.

value.rationale: The object is the full natural 180-flag scheme of the classical Pascal–Kirkman 60-by-60 incidence configuration, not an arbitrary numerical slice. Its complete arithmetic zeta classification for all eleven Frobenius partitions distinguishes rationality of individual geometric objects from rationality of compatible incidences: partitions (6) and (3,3) each have rational Pascal lines and Kirkman points but no rational incident pair. The general extension-field counts and minimal splitting-degree law are usable arithmetic invariants of six-point conic configurations. Scope is deliberately limited to generic reduced configurations, and the source combinatorics themselves are not claimed new.
